scenes.heading: Solving quadratic equations
scenes.say: What number squared gives twenty-five? If you said five, you are only half right. Today you will learn to find both answers to quadratic equations.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A lock that opens with either of two keys
scenes.science: A quadratic equation usually has two solutions
scenes.breaks: Some quadratics have only one solution, and some have none at all.
scenes.say: Picture a lock that opens with either of two keys. A quadratic equation is like that lock. Most have two solutions, and each one makes the equation true. Stop after one and you have only done half the job. But careful: some have just one solution, and some have none.

scenes.heading: x² = k
scenes.say: For x squared equals twenty-five, x is five or negative five, because both square to twenty-five. If the number is positive, there are two answers, plus or minus its square root. If it is zero, there is one. If it is negative, there are none.
scenes.caption: For x² = 25, x is 5 or −5, because both square to 25. If k is positive: two answers, ±√k. If k = 0: one. If k is negative: none.

scenes.heading: The null factor law
scenes.equation: If a × b = 0, a = 0 or b = 0
scenes.say: The null factor law says: if two things multiply to give zero, at least one of them is zero. It only works when one side of the equation is zero.

scenes.heading: Factorise, then solve
scenes.question: Solve x² = 2x + 8.
scenes.say: Solve x squared equals two x plus eight. First make one side zero. Factorise: x minus four, times x plus two. Set each bracket to zero. So x is four or negative two.
scenes.caption: Solve x² = 2x + 8. Make one side zero. Factorise: (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0. Set each bracket to zero. So x = 4 or x = −2.

scenes.heading: Solutions are x-intercepts
scenes.say: Here is the graph of y equals x squared minus x minus six. First the grid, then the curve. Where does it cross the x-axis? At negative two and three. Those are exactly the solutions of x squared minus x minus six equals zero.
scenes.caption: The graph of y = x² − x − 6 crosses the x-axis at −2 and 3. Those are the solutions of x² − x − 6 = 0.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Most quadratic equations have two solutions. Square roots come in pairs. Make one side zero, factorise, then set each factor to zero. Never divide by x. And the solutions are where the graph crosses the x-axis. Now try the practice questions!
